item.stem:
One thousand people selected at random were questioned about smoking and drinking. The results of this survey are summarized in the table below. Calculate the probability that a randomly selected respondent drinks and smokes.

| | Smokers | Non-smokers |
| :--- | :---: | :---: |
| Drinkers | 320 | 530 |
| Non-drinkers | 20 | 130 |

0.032 or similar answers involving place value error.

reference_items.subject: Advanced Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
In the ΔABC the altitudes BN and CM intersect at point S. The measure of ∠MSB is 40° and the measure of ∠SBC is 20°. Write a PROOF of the following statement:

“ΔABC is isosceles.”

Give geometric reasons for statements in your proof.

[Image: Triangle ABC with altitudes BN and CM intersecting at S]

descriptors:
Correct proof. Proves that ∠B = ∠C using the following facts:

• the sum of angles in any triangle is 180°.
• if two angles of a triangle are equal, the triangle is isosceles.
and possibly also uses:
• vertically opposite angles are equal.
• supplementary angles add to 180°.
The concept of congruence is not used.
As code 20 but somewhere in the proof uses the fact that some triangles: e.g. triangles BCM and CBN, OR triangles BMS and CNS, are congruent.
All other fully correct and complete proofs.
As in codes 20-21 shows ∠B and ∠C are equal giving steps in logical order, but omits one step or one reason or gives one incorrect reason.
As in codes 20-21 shows ∠B and ∠C are equal, states correct geometric facts but not in a logically correct order.
Other responses with minor errors.
Shows measures of angles correctly on figure but no geometric facts mentioned or argumentation given.
Incorrect argumentation and/or includes more than one incorrect geometric fact, step, or reason.
"Proof" is circular; makes use of statements which are equivalent to what is to be proven.
Other incorrect responses.
Crossed-out, illegible, or impossible to interpret.
BLANK

reference_items.scoring_notes: Note: To be considered correct, all responses must include mention of all geometric facts used, all calculations made, and a conclusion

reference_items.subject: Advanced Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
For every natural number n, 1^2 + 3^2 + ... + (2n - 1)^2 = (n(4n^2 - 1))/3

To prove this by MATHEMATICAL INDUCTION, what are the essential steps that will need to be carried out? (Do not do the actual proof.)

descriptors:
Correct description of the two steps involved in the proof (i.e., verbal or symbolic statements) equivalent to:
Step 1: Prove that the statement is true for n = 1.
Step 2: Prove if the statement is true for any natural number n = k, then it also is true for n = k + 1.
Describes Step 2 correctly but omits Step 1 or describes it incorrectly (e.g., "prove for n = 0", or "we must prove it for some small number")
Gives correct proof of statement by induction with or without general statement of the induction method, or performs Step 2 correctly but omits Step 1, or describes Step 1 incorrrectly
Describes Step 2: Prove that if the statement is true for any natural number n = k, where k is greater than 1, then it also is true for n = k - 1 with an appropriate Step 1.
Other incorrect (including crossed out, erased, stray marks, illegible, or off task)
Blank

reference_items.stem:
Two circles with centres A and B as shown below have radii of 7 cm and 10 cm respectively. If the length of the common chord PQ is 8 cm, what is the length of AB? Show all your work.

[Image: Two intersecting circles with centers A and B]

descriptors: 14.9 or sqrt(84) + sqrt(33) . Method: Pythagorean theorem applied in triangles APS and BPS (S is the midpoint of PQ).

14.9. Method: Trigonometry functions (ratios) used correctly to determine lengths of sides of triangles OR size of angles of triangle that results in determining the length of AB. Note: Most frequently used trigonometric functions are sine and cosine.
Other complete and correct solutions.
Method as in 20 but solution contains a (minor) error in method, or numerical or rounding error.
Method as in 21 but solution contains a (minor) error in method, or numerical or rounding error.
sqrt(84) + sqrt(33) . No work shown.
Other partially correct solutions, with minor error.
Method: Pythagorean theorem applied to ΔAPB which is not a right triangle.
Incorrect use of the Pythagorean theorem in a right triangle.
Figure in booklet has been considered accurate and lengths of segments and/or measures of angles have been determined from the diagram.
All other incorrect responses.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the two-parameter logistic (2PL) model, which TIMSS uses for constructed-response items worth 1 point, in the calibration "Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
